query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing melt-based fabrication of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi with high-pressure cold-spray (HPCS) solid-state deposition will (a) cut solidification segregation to <1 at.% variation across ≥50 µm, (b) convert net residual tensile stress (+150–250 MPa in arc-melted plate) to a near-surface compressive stress of −100 ± 50 MPa, and (c) raise 0.2 % offset yield strength by ≥25 % at room temperature, without loss of ≥5 % uniform elongation.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomised Al20Cr20Fe20Ni20Si20 (at. %) powder, 15–45 µm diameter, spherical, solutionised and water-quenched microstructure.
generation.intervention: High-pressure cold-spray deposition through DeLaval nozzle at 2.5 MPa He, particle velocity 900 ± 50 m s⁻¹, substrate at 200 °C, single-pass build to 3 mm thickness (no post-HIP or heat treatment).
generation.conditions: Room-temperature mechanical testing; component thickness 2–4 mm; deposition on 316L baseplate; powder feed rate 25 g min⁻¹; nozzle traverse 200 mm s⁻¹. Comparable baseline specimens produced by vacuum arc melting and furnace cooling.
generation.structural_mediator: Severe plastic deformation and high strain-rate impact during HPCS generate ultrafine equiaxed grains (≤0.8 µm) and compressive peening stress while avoiding liquid–solid phase separation.
generation.mechanism: 1. No melting → eliminates solute partitioning and dendritic solidification, so compositional gradients collapse. 2. Adiabatic shear and impact-induced recrystallisation refine grains, increasing Hall–Petch strengthening. 3. Shot-peen-like impact imposes near-surface compressive stress, neutralising tensile residual stress typical for melt-cooled parts. 4. Absence of solidification shrinkage and keyhole voids lowers defect density, preserving ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to arc-melted plate: (i) EPMA line-scan segregation amplitude drops from 5–8 at.% to <1 at.%; (ii) sin²ψ XRD shows surface residual stress change from +200 MPa (tension) to −100 ± 50 MPa (compression); (iii) tensile 0.2 %YS increases from 820 ± 30 MPa to ≥1.0 GPa, while uniform elongation remains ≥15 %.
generation.baseline: Vacuum arc-melted AlCrFeNiSi cast plate, furnace-cooled (~5 K s⁻¹), exhibiting dendritic microsegregation, tensile residual stress, and 0.2 %YS ≈820 MPa with 16 % uniform elongation.
generation.boundary: Valid for powder size 10–60 µm, helium or nitrogen carrier, deposition temperatures ≤0.4 Tm (≈450 °C), and section thickness ≤10 mm; may not hold for larger sections or subsequent heat treatments that recrystallise and relax stress.
generation.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of grain refinement and achievable compressive stress depend on nozzle design and powder size distribution; limited prior data exist for high-entropy alloys containing both Al and Si in HPCS.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of dog-bone coupons: Set A by vacuum arc melting + machining; Set B by HPCS under stated parameters. Characterise composition maps (EPMA), residual stress (sin²ψ XRD), grain size (EBSD), porosity (µ-CT), and perform room-temperature tensile tests (ASTM E8). Minimum N=5 per set.
measurements: EPMA Al, Cr, Fe, Ni, Si concentration profiles over 100 µm lines
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if any two of the following occur simultaneously: (1) compositional variation >2 at.% in Set B; (2) near-surface residual stress in Set B not compressive or magnitude <50 MPa; (3) 0.2 %YS of Set B ≤ baseline value or uniform elongation drops by >5 % absolute compared with baseline.
